Sec. 3.1 discusses light axions (ma ≲ 10−3 eV) converting in magnetic fields and states the probability of observing a future NSM event close enough remains low; Sec. 3.2 discusses MeV-scale axions (ma ~ 100–300 MeV) that decay into photons producing a fireball, and notes that "X-ray observations of GW170817 through CALET CGBM, Konus-Wind, and Insight-HXMT/HE, allow to probe the axion-sourced fireball scenario, ruling out regions of the parameter space unconstrained by other arguments." These are distinct scenarios with different couplings and mass ranges, not contradictory statements about the same observable.

The two statements concern different axion regimes, not the same sensitivity claim. Sec. 3.1 is explicitly about 'light axions with masses ma ≲ 10−3 eV' and says for BNS mergers 'the probability of observing an NSM event close enough to probe currently unconstrained regions ... remains extremely low,' while Sec. 3.2 explicitly switches to 'the opposite mass limit, axions with masses ma ≳ 10 MeV' and states 'differently for the case of light axions, multimessenger observations of BNS mergers provide a powerful tool to constrain ... ma ∼ 100−300 MeV.'

The paper explicitly resolves this apparent contradiction by distinguishing between mass regimes; Section 3.1 discusses 'Light axions', while Section 3.2 introduces the GW170817 constraints by stating, 'Finally, differently for the case of light axions, multimessenger observations of BNS mergers provide a powerful tool to constrain weakly-interacting axions with masses m_a ~ 100-300 MeV.'
